method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the writing-l4-rules skill; the s 6(5)(b) notice a court directs a party to give is a regulative rule (PARTY ... MUST ... WITHIN ... HENCE ... MAY ... LEST BREACH ... BECAUSE) and the seat question reads plain facts; no REFUSE (a court or pair of courts the Act does not speak to answers `not covered`, asserted); every opinion the Act leaves to a court asked as an input; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Jurisdiction of Courts (Cross-vesting) Act 1987, Compilation No. 23 (compilation date 2023-02-06, includes amendments up to Act No. 79, 2022), registered as C2023C00038 (Federal Register of Legislation, retrieved 2026-10-13), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A03433.txt. No instrument brought in (none sets a number or date the Act uses).

checks.command: l4 run jcca-party.l4 ; l4 run jcca-cases-party.l4
checks.result: 104 assertions satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings; 1 #TRACE as its expect line says (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. A breached DEONTIC cannot be compared with EQUALS on this l4, so the rule is asserted through CONSIDER ... WHEN FULFILLED and the breach is #TRACEd.

scope: From the party's seat: s 3(1) (definitions used), s 3(2); s 4(1)-(4); s 5(1)-(9); s 6(1)-(5), (7)-(10); s 6A(1)-(3); s 7(1)-(8) and the Schedule; s 8(1)-(3); s 10; s 11(1)-(3); s 12; s 13; s 14(1), (2). Out: ss 1, 2, 3(3), 3(4), 6(6), 6A(4)-(6) (6A(6) definitions folded into inputs), 9, 14(3), 15, 16 (machinery, construction, suspension by Proclamation).
seat: the party to a civil proceeding: usually the claimant who brings it, sometimes the defendant who answers it; an intervener counts (s 3(1))
